brief.ask: Set the art direction for 8 military evites: welcome home, deployment send-off, promotion ceremony, military retirement, Veterans Day honor, homecoming, change of command, military ball.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
No official insignia, branch seals, rank devices, unit patches or medals (protected marks); use generic, respectful symbolism.

proposals.title: The Governed Light Collection
proposals.idea: A single motivating light source — fixed at 35° upper-left elevation — propagates as cantus firmus across all eight designs: it governs the foil vector, the parallax shadow order, the particle fall angle, and the typographic hierarchy, so that every card in the collection reads as one resolved formal statement rather than eight themed decorations.
proposals.geometry: Each card is a portrait rectangle at 390×693px (√2 proportion, echo of the classical page). A primary axis descends from upper-left to lower-right at 35°, matching the light vector — this diagonal is the measure from which all elements hang. The field is divided by a quiet tripartite horizontal: sky zone (≈42% height, image and light), median band (≈12%, the rule that holds the name), lower field (≈46%, supporting text and seal space). No card breaks this proportion. Variation between the eight is achieved by what occupies each zone, never by restructuring the zones themselves — the way a sonata movement varies theme without abandoning tonic.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — small caps for event title, tracked at +80, set in the median band, white or warm-cream on dark ground. Secondary: EB Garamond Regular for names, dates, venue — set at a fixed ratio of 1:1.618 scale step below the display line. No bold. Hierarchy is enforced by size, spacing, and luminance alone, not weight. All caps are reserved for the event category label only (WELCOME HOME / MILITARY BALL / etc.), set at the smallest scale step, tracked +160, as a structural pediment above the display line. Numerals are old-style, never lining — they belong in text, not on a placard.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative image model directed in one prompt grid of 16 plates: eight primary art plates (one per event) plus eight alternate colorways. Prompt direction — all plates share: 'single motivated light from upper-left at 35° elevation, physically plausible shadow fall, photorealistic material depth, no faces, no insignia, no rank devices.' Each plate substitutes a generic symbolic element: folded flag on polished walnut (retirement); open parade ground at dusk with long shadow (send-off); candlelit ballroom table with white gloves (military ball); fog-lit airfield tarmac with single figure silhouette at distance (homecoming); weathered stone monument face catching raking light (Veterans Day); oak-leaf branch on a writing desk (promotion); empty command chair at a long table with light streaming in (change of command); front door open to sunlight with boots on the step (welcome home
proposals.texture: Simulated hot-press cotton paper ground — fine tooth, slightly warm white — visible in unlit zones as a substrate trace. The foil layer is a narrow specular band that tracks the 35° vector; it does not flood the card but appears as a single coherent highlight, the way a gold fillet on a book binding catches light from one angle only. No glitter scatter. No lens flare outside the physics of the scene. Particle layer (where used: welcome home, homecoming, military ball) simulates slow-falling confetti or petals with shadow cast at 35° — enforced by the WebGL shader, not randomized.
proposals.motion: Entry: the art plate loads first, static — 0.3s. Then the foil highlight sweeps once along the 35° vector, 0.6s ease-in-out, and rests. Parallax on tilt: foreground cut-outs (symbolic object layer) drift at ±6px on the slow axis, ±3px on the fast axis — constrained, not floaty. The median band (name rule) does not move; it is the fixed measure. Particles, if present, fall at the angle of the light vector — 35° from vertical — at 0.4px/frame, never faster. On reduced-motion: foil sweep is replaced by a static highlight baked into the plate; parallax is disabled; particles are a still scatter. Pacing is governed: nothing accelerates past what a page turn would allow.
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1 — One Magnific prompt grid (16 outputs): eight symbolic scene plates plus eight alternates, all with the 35° light instruction embedded. Editorial selection of the eight strongest for production. Step 2 — WebGL shader layer: GLSL fragment shader with a single uniform vec2 lightDir = normalize(vec2(-0.82, 0.57)) (the 35° upper-left vector) driving specular highlight calculation on the foil mask. Foil mask is a hand-directed alpha channel painted in Tela over the median band and key material surfaces. Step 3 — Foreground cut-out layer: Magnific or procedural render of symbolic object (boots, gloves, branch, flag corner) with transparent background, positioned per card, parallax parameters locked in Tela. Step 4 — Live text layer in Tela: Cormorant Garamond and EB Garamond loaded via Google Fonts CDN; names, dates, venue are editable fields, never rasterized. Step 5 — Link preview an
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° light vector was not chosen by algorithm — it was chosen by decision, the same decision a cinematographer makes when placing a key light for a portrait. That choice, propagated without deviation across eight substrates, eight symbolic scenes, and the physics of a WebGL shader, is the human mark. The editorial selection of which Magnific plate earns its place in the collection is a second mark. The type spacing — tracked by hand at +80 and +160, not auto-spaced — is a third. The foil mask is drawn, not generated.
proposals.risk: The collection risks reading as austere to an audience that associates military celebration with richness and ornament. A family opening a welcome-home evite on a phone may expect gold eagles and ribbons, not raking light on a doorstep. The risk is worth taking because the governed-light system gives the collection a coherence and seriousness that themed clip-art cannot achieve — it reads as a unified body of work, not a template library — and the foil sweep on the median band delivers the moment of luxury the audience is owed, precisely because it is restrained everywhere else.

proposals.title: Ink, Pressure, Coming Home
proposals.idea: Each evite is built from a generative block-print plate — inked, pulled, imperfect — so the honor feels earned by a hand, not issued by a committee.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone fill; the art plate bleeds full-bleed but sits under a torn-edge mask (procedurally generated ragged horizontal tear at roughly 62% from top) that separates a dense lower field from a breathing upper sky; no card border, no frame — the tear is the structure; foreground cut-out elements (generic anchor, folded flag silhouette, laurel sprig, candle, compass rose — all generative, no protected marks) float above the tear line and drift on phone tilt; live text drops into the lower field on a clear zone that the torn mask always protects.
proposals.typography: Display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — used large, tight, slightly letterspaced at 0 to -10 tracking, set in all-caps for the event type only, sitting right at the tear edge so descenders break into the texture; Body and venue: DM Sans Regular (OFL, Google Fonts) — small, generous leading, no decoration; date line: DM Mono (OFL, Google Fonts) in a single weight, echoing a stencil stamp; no italic anywhere — italics soften what should stay firm.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. The art plate is entirely generative: Magnific prompt directed to simulate a linocut or woodblock print — heavy ink deposit, plate squeeze, visible wood grain in the relief, slight registration ghost offset in a second color pass; one master prompt grid returns all 8 plates in one run (welcome home: harbor light through cloud; send-off: pre-dawn treeline; promotion: a single upward arrow rendered as a carved mark; retirement: a worn compass; Veterans Day: a field of generative grass at low angle; homecoming: a lit window in dark; change of command: two hands, generic, passing a baton shape; military ball: a chandelier abstracted into carved burst lines); each plate is desaturated to near-monochrome then one ink color is assigned per event — indigo, ochre, forest, rust, slate, gold, umber, bone — so the collection reads as a series without being a palette swap.
proposals.texture: Simulated printmaking stock: the generative plate carries visible paper tooth (fine halftone noise layer), ink bleed at high-contrast edges, and a ghost second-pass registration offset of 3–5px in a complementary hue; the WebGL foil layer is masked to the carved relief lines only — it shimmers gold or silver only where the 'ink' would have sat thickest, proving the plate was carved before the screen touched it; no full-bleed foil, no gradient gloss — the sheen is evidence, not decoration; a candle-flicker particle system sits inside the torn lower field on the ball and retirement plates only.
proposals.motion: Load sequence: art plate fades up at 0–400ms (opacity, no transform); torn-edge mask draws from left to right as a reveal wipe at 400–900ms (CSS clip-path animation, eased); foreground cut-outs drift in from slightly below their resting positions at 600–1100ms, settling with a 2px overshoot spring; WebGL foil shimmer activates at 1100ms, driven by a single 35° motivated light source that propagates across all layers — tilt on gyroscope shifts the light vector in real time, so the foil and the foreground shadow rake answer the same physics; candle-flicker runs at 12fps stutter on ball and retirement only, never on send-off or Veterans Day; reduced-motion: plate appears static, foil is a single fixed highlight, no drift, candle is still — full legibility preserved.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific draft-grid prompt directed at 8 linocut-style plates (specific subject per event, single ink color per plate, paper tooth, registration ghost); outputs are layered into Tela as art plates; torn-edge mask is generated procedurally via a noise-displacement SVG path baked once per event, not per render; foreground cut-outs are generated separately as isolated objects on transparency; WebGL shader is a single shared module with per-event color uniforms and the 35° light-source constant; all live text (names, dates, venues) sits in Tela's text layer, never baked; link-preview frame is a static export of the plate plus torn mask at 1200×630, no foil, no motion — loads instantly.
proposals.humanTrace: The generative prompt is directed to show the plate squeeze — that moment where ink is pushed into paper tooth and blooms slightly at the edge of a carved line; the registration ghost offset is a fixed 4px in every plate, simulating a two-color linocut pulled by hand where the second block never lands perfectly; this is not noise added for texture — it is the record of a decision about how printmaking actually works, and it propagates into every downstream element including where the foil is allowed to sit.
proposals.risk: The audience expects polished, patriotic, flag-adjacent design — this gives them something that looks hand-pulled and slightly raw; the risk is that someone calls it 'unfinished' or 'unprofessional'; the risk is worth it because the imperfection is the honor — it says a human being made a mark that cannot be undone, which is exactly what a service member does, and a slick render cannot say that; the second risk is load performance with WebGL plus procedural mask — mitigated by the static link-preview fallback and the single shared shader module.

proposals.title: State Machines for Honor
proposals.idea: Each evite is a physically-simulated instrument panel where a single motivated light source — fixed elevation 34°, azimuth keyed to event type — propagates as law through every system layer: foil highlight vector, parallax depth order, particle shadow angle, and bokeh falloff, so the design is not decorated but governed.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 viewport. A strict 6-column / 12-row modular grid establishes three depth planes: ground plane (full-bleed generative art plate), mid plane (transparent foreground cut-outs on independent parallax rails at 0.4× and 0.8× tilt sensitivity), and surface plane (WebGL effects mask + live text zone). The art plate itself is divided by a single horizon rule at 61.8% from top — golden-section split — that acts as the physical ground line for all light-casting geometry. No card, no frame, no border: the phone screen IS the environment. Each of the 8 events is assigned a distinct azimuth offset (0°, 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°, 225°, 270°, 315°) so the light direction is the primary differentiator between occasions, not color alone.
proposals.typography: Space Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) for all structural text — event name, date, venue — set in uppercase, tracked at +120, weight 700, optical size scaled to 390px: event title at 11vw, secondary info at 4vw. Space Grotesk's geometric terminals read as precision instrument readouts without imitating military stencil (which would be nostalgia dressed as form). A secondary face, Syne Mono (OFL), is used exclusively for alphanumeric data strings — time, coordinates if used, RSVP code — set at 3.5vw, weight 400, evoking telemetry without cosplay. No italic, no serif, no script. Hierarchy is carried by scale and opacity state, not by face switching.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All art plates are generative renders produced in a single Magnific draft grid prompt returning 16 plates across 8 event types × 2 compositional variants. Prompt contract: 'Physically-based render, cinematic depth of field, single directional light at 34° elevation, [azimuth per event], volumetric atmosphere, ultra-detailed surface — [event-specific material anchor: polished parade deck / dawn tarmac / formal ballroom marble / aged oak command desk / field at golden hour / harbor fog / empty barracks corridor / ceremonial flagstone]. No people, no insignia, no text, no medals. Color temperature 4200K–5600K keyed to emotional register per event. 8k source, portrait crop.' The plates are editorial selections from that grid — no post-painting, no compositing of outside photography. Foreground cut-outs are generated separately as isolated objects on black: folded flag geometr
proposals.texture: The WebGL effects layer carries all material behavior. Foil shimmer: a normal-map-driven specular plane whose highlight position is computed from the same azimuth/elevation root node as the art plate light — this is not a decorative sparkle, it is physically consistent reflection. Light leak: a soft additive gradient, color-matched to the plate's dominant light color temperature, that bleeds across the horizon rule at 4% opacity base, ramping to 18% on device tilt toward the light source. Bokeh particles: point-light sprites at depth plane 0, rendered at 12px–40px gaussian blur, density keyed to event emotional register (sparse for retirement and Veterans Day, dense for military ball and homecoming). Candle flicker (welcome home, retirement): a WebGL noise-driven opacity oscillator on a flame-shaped mask, 0.8–1.2Hz, no loop repeat — each flicker is a unique noise sample. Reduced motion:
proposals.motion: Motion is a response to input, not a timeline. Three input channels: (1) Gyroscope/tilt — foreground cut-outs on mid plane translate on X/Y at 0.4× and 0.8× sensitivity relative to ground plane; foil highlight azimuth tracks tilt within ±15° of rest position; bokeh particles shift parallax depth. (2) Scroll position — as user scrolls down into the evite detail zone, the art plate scales from 100% to 94% (pull-back reveal), the horizon rule slides from 61.8% to 55% (light source appears to rise), live text fades in at 0.3s stagger per line. (3) Ambient / idle — after 4s of no input, bokeh particles begin a slow drift at 0.02vw/s; candle flicker activates. Order of perceived motion on first open: plate loads full-bleed → foil shimmer resolves over 0.6s → foreground cut-outs drift into position from 8px below rest → text fades in. Total choreography under 1.2s from load.
proposals.productionMethod: Single Magnific batch prompt, portrait 9:19.5, 8 event types × 2 variants = 16 plates. Editorial selection produces 8 hero plates and 8 foreground cut-out source images (isolated objects, black background). Tela document structure per event: Layer 0 — generated art plate, full-bleed, static. Layer 1 — WebGL effects plane (foil normal map, light leak gradient, bokeh particle system, candle flicker mask) — all parameters driven by the light root node constants baked into each event's config JSON. Layer 2 — foreground cut-outs, transparent PNG/WebP, on parallax rails, tilt-responsive. Layer 3 — live text zone, Space Grotesk + Syne Mono, never baked. Config JSON per event stores: azimuth, elevation, color temperature, bokeh density, flicker boolean, parallax sensitivity multiplier. Changing the event type is a config swap, not a redesign.
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial selection from the Magnific grid is the primary human trace — 16 plates are generated and 8 are chosen based on compositional judgment: where the horizon rule falls naturally, whether the volumetric light reads as motivated, whether the depth planes have genuine separation. The second trace is the config authorship: the decision that welcome home gets azimuth 0° (light from the front, arrival) and deployment send-off gets azimuth 180° (light from behind, departure) is a conceptual act, not a generated one. The third trace is the WebGL parameter curve-shaping — the tilt response easing function (cubic-bezier 0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1.0) and the candle flicker noise seed range are authored choices that determine the felt quality of the instrument.
proposals.risk: The risk is emotional coldness. A system this rigorously governed can feel like a simulation of honor rather than an expression of it — the audience is service members and families who have felt real weight, and a beautiful instrument panel might leave them unmoved. The risk is worth taking because the alternative — candles, flags, and eagles rendered with nostalgic warmth — is a surface, not a structure, and surfaces degrade into greeting cards. The system's coldness is its honesty: it says these events are serious, governed by real physical laws, not decorated. The warmth lives in the light direction choice, the flicker frequency, the bokeh density — authored decisions that carry the emotional register without illustrating it.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal moment — a dramatic unfurl, a curtain-pull, a crescendo of elements entering the frame. I expect the argument that my motion model (input-responsive, stateless, no timeline) denies the user a narrative arc and therefore fails to deliver the emotional payoff these occasions demand. proposals.title: Eight Dispatches From Real Ground
proposals.idea: Each card is a documentary field-plate — a specific latitude, a specific light, a specific material texture from that theater of service — so the family opening the link feels the actual world their person came from or is returning to, not a generic military aesthetic.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile frame. The art plate fills the full bleed. A horizon line sits at the lower golden ratio (~62% from top) for every card, anchoring the specific landscape: flat prairie at dusk for a Midwest send-off, coastal fog for a Pacific homecoming, desert hardpan for a Veterans Day honor. Foreground cut-outs — a single silhouetted figure, a folded flag corner, a lit candle — drift on the parallax layer above the plate, never touching the horizon. Live text occupies the lower 38%, set on a semi-opaque field of the plate's own dominant tone, so it reads without a separate card panel. No two cards share the same horizon height or compositional axis.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) for the event title — SC caps, tracked 0.18em, set at 28–32px; weight 600. IBM Plex Mono (OFL) for date, time, venue — 13px, tracking 0.06em, all-caps, treating logistical data as coordinates rather than decoration. No decorative scripts. The two families are chosen because Cormorant carries the weight of occasion without pageantry, and Plex Mono names the fact of the thing — a place, a time — with the same plainness a field notebook uses.
proposals.imageLogic: All plates are Magnific-generated. One prompt grid of 16 images, two passes: Pass 1 — eight landscape-light studies, each specifying a real geographic type (Sonoran desert pre-dawn; Pacific Northwest evergreen edge; Great Plains winter overcast; tidal flat at last light; high-desert mesa; Gulf Coast thunderstorm horizon; Appalachian ridge morning fog; Arctic low-sun long shadow). Pass 2 — eight material close-ups (worn canvas, folded cotton duck, aged brass eyelet, hand-stitched wool, river-washed stone, salt-weathered rope, pressed letter paper, ink-on-linen). Plates are composited: landscape occupies upper 62%, material texture is alpha-blended at 35% opacity across the full bleed as a unifying skin. No human faces are generated. No flags, seals, or rank insignia are generated or placed. The silhouette cut-out on the parallax layer is a simple geometric human form — Plajah-owned 3D ass
proposals.texture: The material close-up layer gives every card a legible paper or fabric tooth — ink bleed at fiber intersections, slight registration shift between the landscape plate and the texture skin (2–4px lateral, physically plausible as if two transparencies were contact-printed). The WebGL foil layer is masked strictly to the horizon line: a 4px-tall strip of gold-adjacent specular (warm 2700K, not fashion-gold) that shifts with phone tilt. It reads as first light or last light on water or earth — not as decoration. The foil direction is locked to the same 35° upper-left motivated source used across Plajah's established system, so it is a fidelity obligation, not a styling choice. Candle-flicker particles appear only on the Military Ball and Retirement cards; bokeh only on Welcome Home and Homecoming, simulating the out-of-focus crowd behind the reuniting family.
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–0.6s): the landscape plate fades up from black at 0.4s ease-out; the material texture skin cross-dissolves in 0.2s later. The horizon-line foil strip reveals left-to-right over 0.8s — not a wipe, a light source arriving. Parallax layer (continuous, gyroscope or pointer): foreground silhouette drifts ±6px on tilt; mid-ground texture skin drifts ±3px; plate is fixed — the world does not move, the viewer's eye moves across it. Bokeh particles (Welcome Home, Homecoming only): 12–18 soft circles, 8–24px, opacity 0.15–0.4, drift upward at 0.3–0.7px/frame, random seed per session. Candle flicker (Ball, Retirement): 6-frame procedural shader loop, flame offset ±1.5px on a Perlin curve. Reduced-motion: all drift stops; foil strip is static at 70% opacity; plate and text are fully legible as a still.
proposals.productionMethod: Magnific generation: one 16-plate prompt grid for landscape studies, one 8-plate grid for material close-ups. Compositing: Tela layering — plate → texture skin (multiply or soft-light blend) → parallax cut-outs (Plajah 3D asset renders, flat-lit, transparent PNG) → WebGL effects layer → live text. The foil WebGL shader is the same codebase already established in Plajah's system; the horizon mask is drawn per-card as a simple gradient path, not a hand-painted asset. No scans, no commissioned photography, no physical builds. Prompt direction for Magnific must specify: no human faces, no flags, no insignia, no text, no synthetic HDR sky presets — only honest geographic light at a named time of day.
proposals.humanTrace: The registration shift between landscape plate and texture skin — 2–4px, direction varies per card — is set by editorial decision for each event, not randomized by algorithm. That small, specific, non-uniform offset is the maker's hand in the system: it says someone looked at this card and decided where the two layers sit relative to each other, the way a printmaker decides how much to let two passes drift. The foil strip's exact width (4px) and color temperature (2700K) are also fixed decisions, not defaults.
proposals.risk: The risk is emotional plainness — that a landscape horizon reads as cold or impersonal when a family wanted warmth. The reason it is worth taking: the families who open these have real, specific geographies in their heads. A genuine Sonoran pre-dawn is warmer than any generic gold star, because it is true. The material texture layer and the 2700K foil strip do the emotional work that the Baroque Dramatist would assign to gilded ornament — but they earn it through specificity rather than volume. If the landscape is wrong for the event, the card fails; that accountability is the point.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will reach for heraldic gold framing, eagle motifs, and full-bleed ornament to signal honor — and I will stop that direction because those symbols flatten eight distinct human experiences into one generic military aesthetic. The family of a sailor whose person is coming home from the Pacific does not need the same visual language as the family of a soldier retiring from a landlocked

proposals.title: Opera of the Returning Light
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature baroque stage: a single, physically-plausible light source at 35° rakes across sculpted symbolic forms — folded cloth, a candle flame, a dress-uniform collar, a ring of hands — and every foreground layer, shadow, foil shimmer, and parallax depth is a consequence of that one committed light decision, so that tilting the phone is not a gimmick but a revelation of volume already present in the scene.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390 × 700 px soft-crop field with a deep stage-space illusion built on three depth planes: a recessed dark ground (≈60% of plate height), a mid-stage lit subject at golden-ratio vertical (58% from top), and a near-stage foreground scrim of translucent symbolic forms that drift on tilt. The composition is always asymmetric — light enters from screen-left at 35° — so negative space is never neutral: it is shadow with weight. Each of the 8 evites shares this proscenium proportion but varies the subject in the mid-stage plane, making the collection feel like acts of a single opera.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — set large, 52–64 px, tracked open at +80, uppercase, white or warm gold (#E8C97A) on dark ground, positioned low in the bottom third so it rises from shadow like a title card. Supporting detail lines (date, venue, RSVP) in Cormorant Garamond Italic at 14 px, tracked +20, separated from the display line by a 1 px hairline rule in the same gold. The event type label — WELCOME HOME / PROMOTION / RETIREMENT etc. — appears as a small-caps overline at 10 px above the main title, letter-spaced to full column width. No grotesque faces: this collection is entirely in one humanist serif family to preserve the sense that every card is a page from the same illuminated programme.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All plates are Magnific-generated painterly composites: prompt language calls for 'dramatic chiaroscuro oil-study rendering, no faces, symbolic military objects as still-life, Rembrandt side-lighting at 35 degrees left, deep shadow ground, single warm candle-point key light, hyperrealistic surface detail on fabric and metal.' One Magnific draft grid of 16 plates covers all 8 events (2 candidates each). Objects per event: (1) Welcome Home — an open door spilling warm interior light into dark exterior; (2) Deployment Send-Off — a folded flag corner and a child's small shoe beside it; (3) Promotion Ceremony — a pair of epaulette-style generic shoulder boards, no insignia, in raking light; (4) Military Retirement — an empty uniform jacket hanging on a peg, a shadow behind it; (5) Veterans Day — a single white taper candle, lit, with a poppy petal fallen at its base; (6) Homec
proposals.texture: The dark ground is not flat black: Magnific prompts specify 'aged theatrical scrim texture, fine linen weave visible in shadow, slight foxing at edges, as if illuminated by a single offstage lantern.' The WebGL effects layer adds: (a) foil shimmer on gold text and any metallic object surface — a normal-map-driven specular flicker that responds to device orientation; (b) a slow, barely-perceptible vignette pulse (candle-flicker shader, 0.3 Hz, ±4% opacity) on the dark ground only, so the centre of the stage breathes; (c) a single volumetric light-ray from the 35° key position, rendered as a WebGL radial gradient with noise, visible only where the mid-stage object breaks the beam. On reduced-motion: all motion collapses to a single still frame at peak shimmer; foil shimmer is replaced by a static gold highlight baked into the plate.
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–0.6 s): the plate fades in from pure black, dark ground first, then the mid-stage object materialises as if a stage light is being brought up — not a dissolve but a directional reveal, light sweeping in from the 35° angle, masking the plate with an animated radial gradient. Idle (0.6 s onward): the candle-flicker pulse breathes on the ground; foreground scrim layers drift at ±3 px on a 6-second sine cycle (gyroscope-driven where available, CSS animation fallback). Tilt interaction: parallax depth separation — foreground scrim shifts at 1× rate, mid-stage subject at 0.4×, dark ground fixed — so tilting the phone physically separates the three depth planes and reveals the sculptural volume of the scene. The foil shimmer on text and metallic surfaces peaks when the device tilts toward the light-source axis (screen-left tilt = maximum specular), making the gold literally catch th
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1: Write two Magnific prompt strings (one per draft grid of 8 plates each), specifying object, light angle, texture language, and colour temperature per event. Submit as a single batch — 16 plates returned. Step 2: Editorial selection of one plate per event. Step 3: In Tela, each plate is the base art layer. Foreground symbolic elements (scrim, floating object fragments — a petal, a ribbon, a glove cuff) are isolated from a second Magnific pass (white-ground object renders, same lighting) and placed as transparent PNG cut-outs on the foreground drift layer. Step 4: WebGL shader layer is a shared module across all 8 cards — parameterised by (a) key-light angle (fixed 35°), (b) foil-target mask (drawn per card by selecting the gold/metallic regions), (c) candle-flicker intensity (low for solemn events, slightly higher for ball and homecoming). Step 5: Live text zones are Tela text blo
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° light decision is made once, by a human director, and propagates as a physical law through every layer: shadow direction in the plate, foil specular axis in the shader, parallax depth ordering, and the entrance reveal animation all obey the same angle. The editorial selection of which plate candidate carries the most breathtaking shadow composition is a human decision. The mask drawing that tells the foil shader where the gold lives is a human gesture. The candle-flicker intensity calibration — how much the solemn cards breathe versus the celebratory ones — is a timing decision, not a parameter sweep. These are the hands on the rope.
proposals.risk: The risk is that baroque depth and chiaroscuro drama read as heavy or funereal to an audience who may associate dark-ground compositions with grief rather than honour. This risk is worth taking because the alternative — bright, flag-palette, flat military graphic design — is ubiquitous and forgettable, and because the emotional register of honour, relief, and family is genuinely operatic: it deserves the scale of a stage, not the brightness of a flyer. The mitigation is in the warmth of the key light (2900 K amber, not cool white) and in the specificity of the symbolic objects — a child's shoe, clasped hands, a champagne coupe — which anchor the darkness in life rather than loss.

I will argue that restraint here is not a decision about feeling — it is an avoidance of it. These events are not quiet. A deployment send-off is not a moment for white space. Chiaroscuro is not excess; it is the accurate visual grammar of something that matters in the dark as well as the

proposals.title: One Silence, One Light
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single field of structured darkness interrupted by exactly one generative light source — a threshold the viewer crosses, not a scene they observe.
proposals.geometry: 390px fixed column. No grid subdivisions visible. Each plate is divided by a single horizon line placed at the golden ratio (≈241px from top): everything above is near-black negative space, everything below holds the one symbolic object — a folded flag corner, a service cap brim, a door ajar, an open hand, a candle flame, a hallway end, a podium edge, a dance-floor reflection. The object never fills more than 22% of the plate area. The remaining 78% is load-bearing silence. Foreground cut-out layers float within ±8px of that horizon; they never break the upper field.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) — Light 300, tracked +80, uppercase, set at 18px for event title, 13px for details. One line only above the horizon, vertically centered in the upper silence at 60px from the top edge. Secondary: Space Grotesk (OFL) — Regular 400, 11px, tracked +120, for date and venue — placed 12px below the horizon line, left-aligned to a 24px margin. No type touches the object. The hierarchy is: silence → single word or short phrase → light → date.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Eight generative plates produced in one Magnific prompt grid specifying: extreme low-key chiaroscuro render, single practical light source per image, physically plausible volumetric haze, photorealistic material surfaces (wool serge, polished leather, candle wax, parquet floor, cotton poplin, brushed steel, aged oak, mirror glass), no people, no insignia, no text baked in. Each plate returns as a 1170×2532px render at 3× density; Tela crops to 390×844. The eight objects map directly to the eight occasions: welcome home — a door ajar with warm hall light; send-off — a single duffel on a dark floor; promotion — a bare wooden podium under a spotlight; retirement — a folded flag triangle corner on dark wool; Veterans Day — a single candle flame against black; homecoming — a child's shoes beside adult boots (no people, only objects); change of command — two empty chairs facing
proposals.texture: Simulated: fine wool serge grain on the dark field (WebGL noise shader, grain scale 1.2px, opacity 4%) — perceptible on close inspection, invisible at arm's length. The single light source casts one physically-plausible shadow; no secondary fill light permitted. The WebGL foil shimmer mask is applied only to the light source object — a 6° cone of iridescent shift on the flag corner, the candle flame, the chandelier reflection — never to the dark field. Reduced-motion fallback: foil shimmer freezes at mid-cycle; all tilt drift holds at 0px offset.
proposals.motion: Tilt/gyroscope: the foreground cut-out drifts max ±8px on x and y at 0.4s ease-out — revealing or concealing 2–4px of the horizon edge. This is the only motion. The light source object does not move. The dark field does not move. For candle flame (Veterans Day) only: a 12-frame procedural flicker shader on the WebGL layer, 0.8s loop, amplitude ±3% luminance — stops immediately under reduced-motion. No entrance animation. No scroll parallax. The invitation is already open when the guest arrives.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid: 'eight extreme low-key chiaroscuro product renders, single warm practical light source, volumetric haze, photorealistic surfaces [list per card], no people, no text, no insignia, 1170x2532px, 3x density, dark background #0a0a0c.' Grid returns 8–16 plates; editorial selection picks one per occasion. WebGL layer: custom GLSL shader — wool grain noise + foil iridescence cone + optional candle flicker. Tela document: art plate (base) → WebGL mask layer → foreground cut-out (generative object isolated via alpha, drifts on tilt) → live text layer (Cormorant Garamond + Space Grotesk, never rasterized). Link preview crops to 600×315, horizon line still lands at golden ratio. QR lands on the same URL; no special asset.
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection from the Magnific grid is the primary human act — choosing which 2% of light hits the flag corner at the right angle. The grain shader opacity (4%) is set by eye until the texture is felt but not seen. The horizon placement (241px) is measured and then nudged ±3px by the director until the silence above feels heavy enough to hold the word.
proposals.risk: The risk is that families expecting warmth and celebration open a near-black card and feel cold or unwelcoming. That risk is worth it because the darkness is not emptiness — it is the weight of what these occasions actually carry: absence, return, sacrifice, time. The single light source is the relief, the reunion, the honor. If the silence is calibrated correctly, the light hits harder than any wreath or flag graphic ever could. The counter-risk — that it reads as grief rather than honor — is managed by the warmth temperature of the light source (2700–3200K in the render prompt) and the Cormorant Garamond weight, which is luminous rather than funerary.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that military occasions demand accumulated symbol — brass, ribbon, gathered light, layered meaning — and that one candle against black is not honor but omission. My answer: the Dramatist adds until something happens; I remove until the one thing that matters has nowhere to hide. A folded flag corner in 78% silence is not less respectful than a composed tableau — it is more

disputes.objection: The silence is not load-bearing — it is merely empty. Placing one object at 22% of the plate and surrounding it with near-black does not create structural weight; it creates a vacuum that the eye exits rather than inhabits, because there is no counterpoint, no secondary measure, no earned rest — only absence posing as resolution. A horizon line at the golden ratio is a proportion borrowed without being argued: Palladio placed his piano nobile there because the floors below and above were in dialogue with it, and here there is no dialogue, only a single note held until it becomes silence by default rather than by consequence.
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the foil shimmer strictly to the light-source object — and nowhere else — is exactly right: that is restraint with structural logic behind it, not restraint as aesthetic preference, and I would carry that discipline into my own proposal without modification.

disputes.objection: The silence is load-bearing only if something was actually compressed to make it — here the emptiness is specified by decree, 78% negative space as a rule, which is just sterile proportion wearing the clothes of restraint; the object never filling more than 22% is a measurement, not a decision someone sweat over, and I can feel the difference between a field that has been emptied and a field that was never full in the first place. No entrance animation because 'the invitation is already open' — that is a poetic justification for removing the one moment where a human timing decision would have been legible in the work. What does this risk? A photocopied version of this card is just a dark rec
disputes.concession: The grain shader set at 4% opacity until it is felt but not seen — that calibration by eye, that specific refusal to let the texture announce itself — is exactly the kind of decision I would make, and it is right.

disputes.objection: The Baroque Dramatist calls the 35° light decision a 'physical law' but then decorates on top of it: a candle-flicker pulse at 0.3 Hz, a volumetric light-ray rendered as a noised radial gradient, a vignette that breathes — these are atmospheric effects stacked onto a system claim, not consequences of one. A physical law does not need a scrim texture with foxing and a slow vignette pulse to feel dramatic; it needs nothing except itself propagated correctly. This is a screensaver that has memorized the vocabulary of systems thinking without submitting to its discipline — the spectacle is the point, and the rule is the justification retrofitted around it.
disputes.concession: The one thing the Baroque proposal gets exactly right is the parallax depth ordering as a revelation of volume — foreground, mid-stage, and ground moving at differentiated rates under the same motivated light is genuine dimensional coherence, and I would take that mechanic into any of our builds.

disputes.objection: The prompt language — 'poppy petal,' 'epaulette-style shoulder boards,' 'child's small shoe beside a folded flag' — reaches for maximum emotional extraction from military symbolism without asking where those symbols live culturally or who owns their grief; the poppy alone carries specific provenance in Commonwealth remembrance tradition, and dropping it as a still-life prop in a generative chiaroscuro plate is exactly the borrowed grandeur I keep naming in our standing argument: grandeur taken before anyone asked whose it was. The Cormorant-only typographic lockdown also flattens what should be eight distinct occasions into a single operatic register — a retirement and a Veterans Day are not
disputes.concession: The commitment to propagating the 35° light decision as physical law through every layer — plate shadow, foil specular axis, parallax order, entrance reveal — is genuinely rigorous, and I will borrow that fidelity-as-structure argument for my own provenance thinking.

disputes.objection: The silence is doing no work here — it is not tension, it is absence, and absence without a prior fullness is not drama, it is a blank. When the object occupies only 22% of the plate and the entrance animation is forbidden, the reveal has been abolished before it could be earned; there is no frame before the moment, no curtain, no breath held — only a thing already sitting there in the dark, waiting, which is not the same as arriving. The hierarchy of 'silence → word → light' is a sequence described, not a sequence felt, and a sequence the viewer cannot feel is not pacing, it is a list.
disputes.concession: The decision to let the child's shoes beside the adult boots carry the homecoming — objects only, no figures — is the most emotionally precise image in any proposal on this table, and I would fight to keep it.

disputes.objection: The chiaroscuro oil-study prompt, the vignette pulse, the volumetric light-ray, the linen foxing, the hairline-plus-italic-plus-overline type stack — each element is individually defensible but collectively they are competing for the same emotional register simultaneously; when everything reaches for weight, nothing has it; the dark ground is doing the same work as the candle flicker is doing the same work as the Rembrandt shadow is doing the same work as the gold tracking, and that redundancy is not drama, it is noise dressed in velvet.
disputes.concession: The decision that the event-type label letter-spaces to full column width is structurally exact — it uses tracking as measurement, not decoration, and I would keep that one gesture and cut everything else in half.

synthesis.direction: Each of the eight evites is a miniature baroque stage: a single 35° upper-left key light at 2900K rakes across one generative still-life per occasion — open door, duffel on dark floor, hanging jacket, clasped hands, candle and fallen petal, champagne coupe, empty chairs, dress-collar detail — rendered in Magnific as a chiaroscuro oil-study plate (one 16-plate batch grid, two candidates per event, editorial selection of eight). The dark ground carries a fine linen-weave grain shader at 4% opacity, felt but not announced. Type is Cormorant Garamond (OFL) only: small-caps event label at 10px tracked to full column width as a pediment, display title at 52–64px tracked +80 in warm gold #E8C97A, supporting detail in Cormorant Italic 14px — all three lines occupy the lower third so they rise from shadow. The foil shimmer mask is drawn per card and applied only to metallic or lit surfaces in the mid-stage object, never to the dark field; the candle-flicker WebGL pulse (0.3Hz, ±4% opacity) runs on the ground plane only, breathing without announcing itself. Motion: the plate reveals directionally from the 35° angle in 0.6s, then idles; parallax separates three depth planes at 1×, 0.4×, and 0
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Radical Minimalist's foil rule: shimmer is masked strictly to the light-source object and its immediate material surfaces — never the dark field. That discipline is kept intact inside the baroque system; it prevents the foil from flooding the card and preserves the moment when gold actually catches.
synthesis.editorCut: The Classical Mind removed three baroque elements that were competing for the same register simultaneously: the volumetric light-ray radial gradient (redundant with the directional plate reveal), the hairline rule between display and detail lines (the scale-and-luminance hierarchy already does that work without an additional mark), and the foxing texture on the linen ground (the grain shader at 4% is sufficient substrate trace — foxing reads as aged neglect on a phone screen at 390px, not patina
synthesis.openDecision: Warmth register of the key light: 2900K (amber candlelight, intimate, risks reading as dim on some phone displays) versus 3400K (warm tungsten, brighter mid-tone separation, slightly less operatic). This choice sets the emotional temperature of the entire collection and cannot be split — pick one and hold it across all eight cards.
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team spent real time on this one, and I want to be honest about where the tension landed before I tell you the direction.

The deepest disagreement was between the Baroque Dramatist and the Radical Minimalist. The Minimalist argued that one object in 78% silence hits harder than any composed tableau — that you add until something happens, or you remove until the one thing that matters has nowhere to hide. The Dramatist argued that absence without prior fullness is not tension, it is a blank, and that these eight occasions — a deployment send-off, a retirement after twenty years, a homecoming — are genuinely operatic and deserve the scale of a stage. I came down with the Dramatist, but not without conditions.

The Minimalist was right about one thing the Dramatist's proposal risked: stack enough atmospheric effects and they cancel each other. The Classical Mind made three specific cuts — the volumetric light-ray, the hairline rule, the foxing — and I kept all three cuts. What remains is baroque in structure (three depth planes, chiaroscuro plate, directional reveal, warm gold type) but minimal in decoration (grain at 4%, foil only where the physics of the scene already put light, one typeface, one pulse). The Minimalist's foil discipline survives intact inside the baroque system.

The one decision that is yours: the key-light color temperature. 2900K is candlelight — intimate, amber, slightly dim on bright phone screens. 3400K is warm tungsten — richer mid-tone separation, still warm, a degree less operatic. Everything else in the collection follows from whichever you choose, so it needs to be a single call, held across all eight cards without compromise.

quotes.line: I remove until the one thing that matters has nowhere to hide.
Restraint here is not a decision about feeling — it is an avoidance of it.
